mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate above 4.5% indicates tighter monetary policy, which may lead to decreased borrowing and spending, negatively impacting S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows positive returns in more than 60% of cases when FEDFUNDS exceeds 4.5%, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A rise in unemployment rate by more than 0.3 percentage points over a month signals economic weakness, leading to negative S&P 500 returns in the next 20 days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows positive returns in more than 60% of cases when UNRATE increases by 0.3pp, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A slowdown in retail sales (RSAFS) growth indicates weaker consumer demand, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows positive returns in more than 60% of cases when RSAFS growth slows, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in industrial production (INDPRO) below 100 indicates supply chain issues, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows positive returns in more than 60% of cases when INDPRO is below 100, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: If employment (PAYEMS) grows while unemployment (UNRATE) also rises, it indicates labor market inefficiencies, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows positive returns in more than 60% of cases when PAYEMS grows with rising UNRATE, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: During a monetary tightening cycle, rising federal funds rates (FEDFUNDS) lead to higher borrowing costs, negatively impacting S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows positive returns in more than 60% of cases during monetary tightening, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in housing starts (HOUST) indicates strong demand in the housing market, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows negative returns in more than 40% of cases when HOUST increases, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: High federal funds rates (FEDFUNDS) combined with slowing GDP growth (GDPC1) indicate stagflation, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows positive returns in more than 60% of cases when FEDFUNDS are high and GDPC1 slows, the hypothesis is rejected.
